test_title: PYST 60: RRB Group D - GS (Held On: 23 Dec, 2025 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which statement correctly defines the process of evaporation?

options.text: It changes solids directly into vapors upon heating strongly
It takes place only at the boiling temperature of a liquid
It changes a liquid to gas from the surface below boiling point
It requires the liquid to freeze before changing to the gas form

solution:
The correct answer is __**It changes a liquid to gas from the surface below boiling point**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Evaporation** is a type of **vaporization** that occurs on the **surface** of a liquid as it changes into the **gas phase**. It is fundamentally different from boiling because it occurs only at the **surface** and can happen at **any temperature** below the boiling point of the liquid.
 
• Statement 1 suggests that it changes solids directly into vapors. This process is actually known as **sublimation** (e.g., dry ice or camphor) and does not involve the liquid phase at all. ***Hence, statement 1 is incorrect.***
 
• Statement 2 claims it takes place only at the boiling temperature. This is the definition of **boiling**, which is a **bulk phenomenon** where the entire mass of the liquid transitions to gas. Evaporation, conversely, happens continuously even at **room temperature**. ***Hence, statement 2 is incorrect.***
 
• Statement 3 defines the process correctly as the transition from liquid to gas from the **surface** at temperatures **below the boiling point**. In this process, particles at the surface gain enough **kinetic energy** to overcome the **intermolecular forces** of attraction. ***Hence, statement 3 is correct.***
 
• Statement 4 mentions that the liquid must freeze first. Freezing is the transition from **liquid to solid**, which is the opposite direction of the energy change required for gas formation. ***Hence, statement 4 is incorrect.***

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

__
 
• **Factors Affecting Evaporation:**
 
 
• **Surface Area:** Since evaporation is a **surface phenomenon**, increasing the surface area (e.g., spreading out wet clothes) increases the **rate of evaporation**.
 
• **Temperature:** An increase in **temperature** provides more **kinetic energy** to the particles, allowing a greater number of them to escape into the vapor state.
 
• **Humidity:** It is the amount of **water vapor** present in the air. If the humidity is high, the air cannot hold much more moisture, thus **decreasing** the rate of evaporation.
 
• **Wind Speed:** Higher **wind speeds** move water vapor particles away from the surface, making room for more molecules to evaporate, thus **increasing** the rate.
 
 
 
• **Cooling Effect:**
 
 
• Evaporation causes **cooling**. During the process, the particles of the liquid absorb energy (the **Latent Heat of Vaporization**) from the surroundings to regain the energy lost during evaporation.
 
• Common examples include **sweating** in humans to regulate body temperature and the cooling of water stored in **earthen pots** (matkas) during **summer**.
 
 
 
• **Comparison with Boiling:**
 
 
• While **boiling** is a fast process that occurs throughout the **bulk** of the liquid at a **fixed temperature**, evaporation is a **slow and silent** process occurring only at the surface at **variable temperatures**.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/4f750a2730aad0987b5e719f277ddc90129c657928205c4d3b5aa23049023fa5.png] **Important Points__**

 
• The **Latent Heat of Vaporization** is the heat energy required to change **1 kg** of a liquid into gas at **atmospheric pressure** at its boiling point.
 
• In the context of the **Water Cycle**, evaporation from **oceans, seas, and lakes** is the primary pathway for water to move from the liquid state back into the **atmosphere** as water vapor.
 
• **Vapor Pressure:** Evaporation continues until the **partial pressure** of the vapor in the air reaches the **equilibrium vapor pressure** of the liquid.
</ul
